biggest_catch: You are paid per AUDIO minute, not per working minute - Rev's own page says the average person takes about 4 hours per audio hour while professionals take 2-3, so the headline $0.40-$1.10/audio minute can translate to a low effective hourly wage for beginners.
catches: Per-audio-minute pay is not per-working-minute: Rev's official speed page says an average person takes ~4 hours per audio hour (professionals 2-3 hours).
Rejected or low-graded work pays less or nothing; quality review gates your earnings.
Application waitlist: Rev states signups may be waitlisted due to application volume - you cannot always start immediately.
PayPal only for payouts; PayPal's own transfer limits and fees can apply on your side.

eligibility: 18+; fluent English; strong grammar; pass Rev's grammar quiz and sample transcription/captioning test.
maximize: Cherry-pick short, clear-audio files first - they pay the same per audio minute but take far less working time, and Rev's own speed page names audio quality as the biggest time driver. Build a text-expander snippet library for common phrases, learn Rev's style guide cold to avoid grade penalties, and graduate to captioning work ($0.54-$1.10/audio min floor beats transcription's $0.40). Speed is the whole business model: professionals transcribe an audio hour in 2-3 hours versus 4 for the average person.
